extracted.intended_audience: National Academies / NRC study committee members, report authors, report reviewers, and study staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedures for forming study committees, conducting committee deliberations, drafting consensus reports, and performing independent review of National Academies (NRC) consensus reports to ensure independence, objectivity, and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate range of expertise for the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee must include experts with the specific expertise and experience needed to address the study’s statement of task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members are chosen on the basis of their knowledge and experience in aspects of the topic; the staff reviews literature and consults widely to define areas of expertise. Bringing together recognized experts from diverse disciplines and backgrounds is a strength and is encouraged to foster new ways of thinking about a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of perspectives on the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the overall composition of the committee in terms of different experiences and perspectives so that relevant points of view are reasonably balanced for objectivity and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Having the right expertise is not sufficient; committees should include diverse viewpoints. Point of view or bias is not necessarily a conflict of interest; members are expected to state their views rather than represent organizations. When balance questions arise, adding members to achieve appropriate balance is usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening for conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: All provisional committee members are screened for conflicts of interest in writing and in confidential group discussion; conflicts that could significantly impair objectivity must be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'conflict of interest' means any financial or other interest that could significantly impair the individual's objectivity or create an unfair competitive advantage. Members must disclose professional, consulting, financial connections and pertinent intellectual positions. Appointment is not finalized until review of potential conflicts and bias is complete. Conflicts discovered later may require resignation or public disclosure if unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting and comment on provisional committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional committee lists are posted for public comment in the Current Projects System; nominees complete background and conflict disclosure forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff solicit broad suggestions for potential members, recommend a slate, which is approved in stages and posted for public comment. The provisional members complete background information and conflict-of-interest disclosure; committee balance and conflict discussion is held at the first meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-gathering meetings should be open and soliciting input
rubrics_metrics.description: Information-gathering meetings of the committee are open to the public (with few exceptions) and efforts are made to solicit input from individuals with direct involvement or special knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data-gathering meetings are announced in advance via the Academies Web site; written materials provided by non-officials are maintained in a public access file. Committees should create opportunities such as public comment sessions and solicit comments in writing or via email. Exceptions apply where classified, proprietary, or personal-privacy information is involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance announcement of public meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: An advance announcement of data-gathering committee meetings should be posted—preferably 14 days before the meeting—on the institution’s Web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance notice facilitates public attendance and comment. The chair should also advise attendees of the nature and purpose of the meeting to avoid misinterpretation of discussions as official positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberations and draft products remain confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee deliberations in closed session and all analyses and drafts remain confidential until review is complete and the report is signed off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberations are closed to develop draft findings free from outside influence. Brief public summaries of closed meetings (listing members present, topics discussed, materials) must be posted within 10 days but must not disclose substantive content, conclusions, recommendations, draft reports, or report review comments. Committee members should avoid premature briefings that could undermine independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on committee members' public comments prior to release
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the review process is completed, committee members should limit public comment to the scope of the project, the sponsor and estimated cost, and the makeup of the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction helps prevent impressions that sponsors previewed or approved conclusions. Premature briefings may lock committees into unsupported positions and damage the report's independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent, anonymous external review of reports
rubrics_metrics.description: All reports must undergo rigorous, independent external review by experts whose comments are provided anonymously to the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Academies recruit independent experts with a range of views and perspectives. Reviewers receive the complete draft along with the statement of task and are asked to provide written comments. Review comments are treated as confidential, identifiers removed, and reviewers are asked to return or destroy drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers' confidentiality and anonymity obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Review comments are confidential; reviewers' identities are removed from comments and reviewers should not disclose their comments or the draft manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submitting comments, reviewers are asked to return or destroy the draft manuscript and refrain from disclosing their comments. Names and affiliations of reviewers are made public when the report is released, but their comments remain confidential; reviewers should not divulge comments even after release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report must address the approved study charge and not go beyond it
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the report clearly identifies the study charge and stays within its bounds; the statement of task must be clearly described and all aspects addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a committee finds its charge inadequate, it can petition to modify the task. Reviewers should check whether authors go beyond their charge or expertise and whether all aspects are fully addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings, conclusions, and recommendations must be supported by evidence and argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions and recommendations should be adequately supported by evidence, analysis, and argument; uncertainties should be explicitly recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale should be fully explained with references to literature, analysis of data, and discussion of pros and cons of alternatives. If recommendations are based on value judgments or collective opinion, that should be acknowledged with reasons. Failure to document conclusions and recommendations adequately is a common shortcoming. Recommendations calling for organizational changes or budget increases should be avoided unless specifically called for in the study charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent handling of data and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and analyses should be handled competently and statistical methods applied appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess data treatment and appropriateness of statistical methods; if the report relies on signed papers, those papers should also meet standards for competent analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful treatment of sensitive policy issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensitive policy issues must be treated with proper care, including consideration of advantages and disadvantages of alternatives and consistency across the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include recommendations about reorganization of an agency or creation of a new entity; the report should consider alternatives, including the status quo, and be consistent with other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective exposition and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The report's exposition and organization should be effective and the title appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge clarity, structure, flow, and whether the report communicates its reasoning and findings effectively to its intended audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial tone and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The report should be fair in tone—impartial and devoid of special pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should watch for advocacy posing as analysis, ensuring the report represents evidence-based, balanced conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary and summary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every report must contain a Summary or Executive Summary that clearly and concisely communicates the main message to intended audiences and must not distort or go beyond report content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Executive Summary should typically be less than 800 words and not exceed 1,000 words. A Summary should typically be less than 3,000 words and not exceed 5,000 words unless preceded by an Executive Summary. The Summary must clearly identify the study charge and be consistent with other sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consensus process and handling of dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: Committees should strive for consensus but may include a brief dissent (no more than 5,000 words) as an appendix describing issues of contention and supporting arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissents should be referenced in the introductory text and table of contents, may not address issues outside the study charge, may not misrepresent the majority, and are subject to RRC chair review for appropriateness. Reviewers' comments on a dissent are given to its author but no formal written response is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should distinguish major from minor concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: In providing comments, reviewers are encouraged to distinguish issues of general/major concern from less significant points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps authors prioritize revisions. Reviewers are asked to provide written comments on all aspects but pay special attention to the stated review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must respond in writing to reviewer comments and monitors evaluate responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Each committee must respond to reviewer comments in a detailed 'response to review' that is examined by independent report review monitors to ensure review criteria have been satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to consider all review comments and provide written responses. The monitor (appointed by the RRC) and/or review coordinator evaluate whether responses adequately address reviewers' concerns. The report may not be released until the RRC is satisfied with review completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of review is assessment of soundness and responsiveness to charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Review aims to assist authors in making reports accurate and effective and to ensure reports creditably represent authors and the Academies; reviewers judge evidence and argument soundness and responsiveness to the charge, not whether they concur with findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review fulfills institutional oversight and provides diverse expert reactions to enhance clarity, cogency, and credibility of the final document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on dissemination prior to review completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Drafts, tentative conclusions, and committee deliberations are not official and may not be released to sponsors or the public until review and sign-off are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Premature briefings can undermine independence and lead to accusations of sponsor influence. Committee members should avoid early briefings or media interviews about findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report release conditions and sponsor interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: After sign-off and review completion, the report is transmitted to the sponsor and released to the public; sponsors are not given an opportunity to suggest changes in reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names and affiliations of principal reviewers are made public when the report is released. OCGA and ONPI coordinate congressional and media briefings, with briefings allowed up to 24 hours before public release under guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish evidence-based conclusions from informed judgment in risk assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: In risk assessment studies, committees must clearly distinguish conclusions based on scientific evidence from those based on informed judgment and explicitly identify and justify assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where scientific proof is incomplete, explain how conclusions were reached, identify assumptions, and justify them. Special care is needed in committee assembly, bias discussions, consensus management, minority opinions, and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional oversight of study scope, plan, and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of task, work plan, and budget must be approved by the Executive Committee of the NRC Governing Board and oversight is provided throughout the study to ensure quality control and adherence to scope, schedule, and budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight entities and study staff ensure the committee focuses on its stated tasks; sponsors do not engage in oversight. The Executive Committee may alter tasks or turn down studies not appropriate for the Academies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access practices and meeting records
rubrics_metrics.description: Data-gathering meetings are on-the-record; chairs should set ground rules and ask members to state relevant background in open session; public access files contain materials presented and are available for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A brief summary of closed meetings (listing committee members present, topics discussed, materials made available) must be posted within 10 days; summaries must not disclose substantive content or review comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of staff in report preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff assist in research, writing, integrating contributions, and ensuring consistent style and format but do not insert their personal conclusions or recommendations; final conclusions and recommendations are those of the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff ensure procedures are followed and the study stays on schedule and budget. The 'author of record' is the entire committee and individual authorship is generally not credited; reports and copyrights are property of the National Academy of Sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsupported organizational or budgetary recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations calling for organizational changes or budgetary increases should be avoided unless specifically called for in the study charge and adequately supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such recommendations require particularly strong supporting evidence and justification; failure to document backing is a common shortcoming of draft reports.
